entries.name: Controlling discrete semilinear wave equations toward flocks
entries.abstract: We construct pointwise bounded controls that steer a finite, periodic, fully actuated active harmonic lattice with Rayleigh-Helmholtz velocity forcing to flock states in finite time. In our setting, an initial Lyapunov-feedback phase brings the velocities and elastic forces into a prescribed small neighborhood of zero. Then, subsequent trajectory planning and cancellation of the known drift achieve exact arrival at a moving flock. For prescribed stationary or moving profiles satisfying a strict control-admissibility condition, a two-stage interpolation reaches the target. We provide explicit sufficient time intervals for the stages following the initial feedback phase. Finally, we formulate the associated minimum-time problem and its formal Hamilton-Jacobi equation, leaving the continuity of the value function open.

entries.name: Affine standard Lyndon words
entries.abstract: In this note, we establish the convexity and monotonicity for affine standard Lyndon words in all types, generalizing the $A$-type results of arXiv:2305.16299. We also derive partial results on the structure of imaginary standard Lyndon words and present a conjecture for their general form. Additionally, we provide computer code in Appendix that, in particular, allows to efficiently compute affine standard Lyndon words in exceptional types for all orders.

entries.name: Legendrian doubles, twist spuns, and clusters
entries.abstract: Let $λ$ be a Legendrian link in standard contact $\mathbb{R}^3$, such that $L_1$, $L_2$ are two exact fillings of $λ$ and $\varphi$ is a Legendrian loop of $λ$. We study fillability and isotopy characterizations of Legendrian surfaces in standard contact $\mathbb{R}^5$ built from the above data by doubling or twist spinning; denoting them $Λ(L_1,L_2)$ or $Σ_\varphi(λ)$ respectively. In the case of doubles $Λ(L_1,L_2)$, if the sheaf moduli $\mathcal{M}_1(λ)$ admits a cluster structure, we introduce the notion of mutation distance and study its relationship with the isotopy class of the Legendrian surface. For twist spuns $Σ_\varphi(λ)$, when $\mathcal{M}_1(λ)$ admits a globally foldable cluster structure, we use the existence of a $\varphi$-symmetric filling of the Legendrian link to build a cluster structure on the sheaf moduli of the twist spun by folding. We then use that to motivate, and provide evidence for, conjectures on the number of embedded exact fillings of certain twist spuns. Further, we obstruct the exact fillability of certain twist spuns by analyzing fixed points of the cyclic shift action on Grassmanians.

entries.name: Support measures in fractal geometry
entries.abstract: We introduce two novel families of geometric functionals-basic contents and support contents-for investigating the fractal properties of compact subsets in Euclidean space. These functionals are derived from the support measures arising in connection with the general Steiner formula due to Hug, Last, and Weil, and offer new tools for extracting geometric information beyond classical fractal dimensions. The basic contents are constructed from the support measures of the set itself, while the support contents arise from those of its parallel sets. Associated scaling exponents characterize the asymptotic behavior of these measures as the resolution parameter tends to zero. We establish a fundamental connection between the maximum of the basic scaling exponents and the outer Minkowski dimension. The proof relies on the novel notion of outer box dimension. Furthermore, we explore how support contents supply aggregated information on geometric features that is provided separately by the basic contents, and how they relate to fractal curvatures and complex dimensions. Our results provide a deeper understanding of which geometric aspects actually contribute to fractal invariants such as the (outer) Minkowski content. We provide some illustrative examples.

entries.name: Posterior error bounds for prior-driven balancing in linear Gaussian inverse problems
entries.abstract: In large-scale Bayesian inverse problems, it is often necessary to apply approximate forward models to reduce the cost of forward model evaluations, while controlling approximation quality. In the context of Bayesian inverse problems with linear forward models, Gaussian priors, and Gaussian noise, we use perturbation theory for inverses to bound the error in the approximate posterior mean and posterior covariance resulting from a linear approximate forward model. We then focus on the smoothing problem of inferring the initial condition of linear time-invariant dynamical systems, using finitely many partial state observations. For such problems, and for a specific model order reduction method based on balanced truncation, we show that the impulse response of a certain prior-driven system is closely related to the prior-preconditioned Hessian of the inverse problem. This reveals a novel connection between systems theory and inverse problems. We exploit this connection to prove the first a priori error bounds for system-theoretic model order reduction methods applied to smoothing problems. The bounds control the approximation error of the posterior mean and covariance in terms of the truncated Hankel singular values of the underlying system.

entries.name: Repair-Based Duality for Distributionally Robust Optimization via Conditional-Moment Optimal Transport
entries.abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) models often admit dual representations that replace optimization over probability distributions with more tractable formulations, but estab- lishing primal-dual equality can be challenging when ambiguity sets involve conditional moment restrictions, noncompact uncertainty spaces, or unbounded losses. We study these questions through the conditional-moment optimal transport (CM-OT) framework, which encompasses transport-, divergence-, and jointly perturbed DRO models. Our main contribution is a repair- based sufficient condition for primal-dual equality. The approach constructs feasible couplings from nearly feasible ones by mixing with suitable reference couplings, while a local conditional uniform integrability condition on positive-loss tails ensures that the resulting repairs do not incur a nonvanishing loss in objective value. This establishes the closedness of the associated perturbation value function without relying on compactness or conventional interiority condi- tions. We further distinguish primal-dual equality from the additional steps required to obtain pointwise dual representations, providing conditions under which essentially bounded measurable conditional-moment multipliers can be replaced, at the level of optimal values, by bounded continuous multipliers and under which optimization and integration can be interchanged. Finally, we apply the framework to a class of DRO models combining divergence-based ambiguity with distributional calibration, including contextual resource-allocation and reliability applications.

entries.name: Ultracontact algebras and stack systems
entries.abstract: We study the class of structures that, in a way, generalize various approaches to the contact relation on Boolean algebras.

entries.name: The Threshold Breakdown Point
entries.abstract: We introduce a novel approach to finite sample robustness that avoids the pessimism of traditional breakdown analyses. We define the threshold breakdown point, the smallest contamination fraction needed to induce a prescribed deviation, and the finite sample $m$-sensitivity, the worst-case deviation that an estimator can incur after $m$ observations are contaminated. We derive these measures for commonly used $M$-estimators, their standard errors and related test statistics. This allows us to extend the decision breakdown point of Zhang (1996) to obtain general breakdown characterizations for hypothesis testing, and show how these notions connect to finite sample counterparts of the power and level breakdown functions of He, Simpson and Portnoy (1990). We complement our work with an inferential framework for the threshold breakdown and $m$-sensitivity that yields consistency and asymptotic normality results, as well as a valid multiplier bootstrap for uncertainty quantification. We illustrate the practical utility of our methods in various numerical examples and an application to a two sample testing problem for a blood pressure dataset.

entries.name: Logarithmic oscillatory multipliers and log-subdyadic square functions
entries.abstract: We develop square-function estimates for Fourier multipliers whose local oscillation scale is \[ ρ(R)=\frac{R}{(\log R)^{γ-1}}, \qquad γ>1. \] This scale lies strictly between the dyadic scale and every fixed power-subdyadic scale at high frequency. For high-frequency symbols satisfying a localized Sobolev condition on balls of radius comparable to $ρ(R)$, we prove a pointwise square-function estimate and a weighted $L^2$ multiplier inequality. After adjoining a smooth compactly supported low-frequency part, we derive unweighted $L^p$ bounds. The weighted estimate is governed by a logarithmic geometric maximal operator which is strongly bounded above the critical $L^r$ threshold, satisfies weak type at the critical equality, and fails even weak type below it. As a model application, consider \[ L(ξ)=\frac12\log(e^2+|ξ|^2), \qquad m_{γ,β}(ξ)=L(ξ)^{-β}e^{iL(ξ)^γ}. \] For $p=2$, the associated multiplier is bounded on $L^2$ for every $β\geq0$. For $1<p<\infty$, $p\neq2$, it is bounded on $L^p$ under the sufficient condition \[ β> d(γ-1)\left|\frac12-\frac1p\right|. \] At the critical equality we obtain the corresponding Lorentz endpoint estimates.

entries.name: On triviality and scalar curvature estimation of gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons
entries.abstract: In this study we have explored gradient $h$-almost Yamabe solitons on both compact and complete non-compact Riemannian manifolds. We have established several sufficient conditions for the triviality of such solitons with respect to integral inequalities involving the scalar curvature and the soliton function. In this regard, we have acquired scalar curvature estimation under certain $L^1$ and $L^2$ integrability conditions, and defined signal of the function $h$. Our results extend and refine former works on almost and $h$-almost Yamabe solitons, and characterize the geometric structures of generalized Yamabe solitons.

entries.name: Local solutions to hyperbolic systems with fractional dissipation
entries.abstract: We study the local Cauchy problem for a class of hyperbolic quasilinear evolution systems with fractional dissipation and commutators of the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^α$ with arbitrary $α\in(0,1)$ in the framework of Sobolev spaces. The analysis is motivated by the compressible Euler alignment system with singular communication weights. We show that the contribution of the commutators to the energy is absorbed by the dissipation. Our approach does not rely on the cancellation condition previously used to recover the coercivity of the highest order nonlocal terms. We further show that the commutator term induces a loss of regularity in the stability estimates, preventing the standard contraction argument from being applied. Therefore, we instead establish the relative compactness of the solution operator and apply Schauder's fixed point theorem to provide local existence for large initial data. The resulting theory identifies the obstacles to deduce local uniqueness in the presence of commutators.

entries.name: Stochastic Operator Algebras: Intrinsic Cumulant Geometry
entries.abstract: If an orthogonal projection splits a random vector into independent parts, every mixed cumulant across the cut vanishes. For a family of cuts we identify the subspaces on which higher cumulants can survive. A distance bound on vectors characterizes when square-integrable defects at the individual cuts admit a simultaneous correction by a Hilbert tensor. The criterion is the same in every integer degree $r\ge3$ and can be tested on Hilbert-space-valued random variables. For laws fixed by random recombination, uniform cutting supplies the moment asked for by Courtade. The minimum dimension of a nonzero finite-dimensional common reducing subspace determines the optimal fourth-moment ratio. A separate application to polynomial optimization characterizes the $r^{-2}$ push-forward rate on a convex body by the boundary area of sublevel sets at regular minima.

entries.name: Punctured Wilson--Evolving Sets and Root Identities for Massive Kirchhoff Forests
entries.abstract: Let $F_q$ be the rooted forest sampled by Wilson's algorithm for a finite reversible Markov chain killed at rate $q$. We express the probability that $k$ prescribed vertices are roots as a product. For the $i$th factor, start an evolving set from the singleton consisting of the $i$th vertex, in the domain obtained by removing the preceding $i-1$ vertices. The factor is the probability that the set contains its starting vertex at an independent exponential time of rate $q$. These factors are the successive Schur-complement pivots of the determinantal root kernel. The construction couples the walk up to its exit from a domain with the evolving set biased by its mass. For the ordinary evolving set, the expected mass at that time divided by the initial mass is the probability that the walk has not yet left the domain. We use the probability that a second walk hits the first Wilson branch to bound the probability that two vertices belong to the same component. For a symmetric transition kernel, the expected size of the component of any vertex is at most $(1+1/q)^2$. Under a Gaussian heat-kernel upper bound with exponent $ν>4$, we also obtain spatial decay on the scale $q^{-1/2}$, up to a finite-volume correction.

entries.name: Power-saving density bounds for $K$-point configurations in $\mathbb{Z}^d$
entries.abstract: Let $d,K,N\in \mathbb{N}$ with $K\geq 3$ and $d\geq 4K+4$. Let $Δ\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be the vertex set of a nondegenerate $(K-1)$-simplex, and let $A\subseteq[N]^d$ contain no nontrivial similar copy of $Δ$. We prove that \[ |A|\ll_{Δ,d} N^{d-c_{Δ,d}}, \] improving upon a polylogarithmic bound due to Magyar. We combine an induction-on-scale argument with the circle method, and we introduce a ``cut operator'' method to decouple the weighted exponential sum over the system of quadratic forms describing the simplex. Our proof combines ideas from graph theory, functional analysis, and the geometry of numbers. In the process, we apply Finner's fractional form of Hölder's inequality, the analytic large sieve, and Kim's mean value formula for primitive lattice flags.

entries.name: Universal existence and generic uniqueness for quadratic BSDE systems in a two-player stochastic differential game
entries.abstract: We study two-dimensional quadratic backward stochastic differential equations in the augmented natural filtration of a one-dimensional Brownian motion. The generator has components $q_{θ,i}(z)=z_i(z_1+z_2)-α_i z_i^2/2$, $i=1,2$, where $θ=(α_1,α_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$. In the associated stochastic differential game, two players choose efforts $u_1,u_2$, the common state has drift $u_1+u_2$, and player $i$ pays $u_i^2/2$ per unit time and has risk sensitivity $α_i-1$. For every bounded terminal payoff vector $ξ$, which may depend on the entire state path, $(Y,Z)\mapsto Z$ is a bijection from solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ to Nash equilibria in BMO controls. Whether the risk-neutral system ($α_1=α_2=1$) is well posed for every such $ξ$ was left open in [Jackson (2023), Section 6.4]. For $α_1α_2\ne0$ with $α_1^{-1}+α_2^{-1}=1$, existence and uniqueness in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every bounded $ξ$ were established in [Fan, Hu and Tang (2025), Corollary 2.25]. We prove that every bounded $ξ$ admits a solution in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$ for every $θ\in\mathbb{R}^2$. The solution is unique for every bounded $ξ$ if $(α_1-1)(α_2-1)=1$, but for every $θ$ with $(α_1-1)(α_2-1)\ne1$, we construct a bounded $ξ$ admitting at least two distinct solutions in $\mathcal{S}^\infty\times\mathrm{BMO}$. Nevertheless, for each $θ\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $M>0$, uniqueness holds on a dense $G_δ$ subset of the space of $[-M,M]^2$-valued terminal conditions equipped with the topology of convergence in probability. Moreover, if $ξ_n$ in this space converges in probability to a point $ξ$ of this subset, every choice of solutions for $ξ_n$ converges to the unique solution for $ξ$ in $\mathcal{S}^p\times\mathcal{H}^p$ for every $1\le p<\infty$.

entries.name: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
entries.abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and often accelerates in practice. One of our main contributions is to disprove the conjecture that it is uniformly accelerated on strongly convex functions. We develop a taxonomy of memory mechanisms by window length and forgetting rate. We consider exact subspace methods whose memory is a window of recent gradients and steps plus finitely many fixed cumulative sums. For this class, uniform acceleration requires either a window of length at least of order the square root of the condition number or a sum that forgets at a rate at least of order the inverse square root. For one fixed-factor filter pair with a bounded window this forgetting scale is necessary and sufficient up to constants. SESOP remembers too much and the plane form of conjugate gradients too little: neither is uniformly accelerated, even on infinitely differentiable functions quadratic near the minimizer. A short window converges locally quadratically over blocks when the Hessian is Lipschitz near the minimizer and equals a multiple of the identity plus a low-rank term there. Constructive upper bounds reach this forgetting scale without problem constants. Geometric filter pairs created at fixed times give uniform acceleration with logarithmic memory, also with inexact subproblems. A single pair with a smoothly adapted factor uses two vectors and attains an accelerated linear rate up to a prefactor polynomial in the condition number.

entries.name: Two-scale band geometry and ballistic transport for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
entries.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with bounded limit-periodic potentials. If the nested periodic approximants satisfy $\|V-V_n\|_\infty=o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-ηp_n})$, with $η>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, then the rescaled Heisenberg position has a nonzero strong limit on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. In contrast to earlier continuum results requiring exponential accuracy in $p_{n+1}$, the exponential weight here involves only $p_n$; the ratios $p_{n+1}/p_n$ may be unbounded. Folding identifies each ordered large-cell band, away from symmetry momenta, with a fixed translated small-cell band. This confines near-collisions of all bands to a common neighborhood controlled at the smaller period. A period-uniform quadratic-form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a graph-norm comparison linear in the potential error then give the limiting velocity. Moments of orders $0<r\le4$ have two-sided ballistic growth as a corollary. An explicit example separates the two approximation conditions.

entries.name: Deformations and Local Geometry of Lie Triple System Morphisms
entries.abstract: In this paper, first we study the deformations, stability and rigidity of Lie triple system morphisms by means of higher derived brackets and augmented Yamaguti cohomology. The vanishing of the first cohomology gives formal and local inner rigidity. The vanishing of the second cohomology removes the formal extension obstructions and, in finite dimension over $\mathbb{R}$, gives local smoothness and stability under simultaneous perturbations of the two products. Next, we establish the relationship with Lie algebra homomorphisms in each part of the theory. The universal enveloping Lie algebra identifies a Lie triple morphism with a grading-preserving Lie homomorphism. We obtain the corresponding first cohomology isomorphism, the equivalence of formal and smooth deformations, and a stability result for graded Lie bracket perturbations. For Lie triple products induced by binary Lie brackets, we construct a comparison of differentials and obstruction classes. Under perfectness and a zero-centralizer condition, the local morphism spaces coincide. Finally, we relate triple subsystem graphs to graded Lie subalgebra graphs and compare their normal differentials.

entries.name: Certificate-Based Verification of Pulsed Field Ablation Models
entries.abstract: Computational models of cardiac pulsed field ablation predict the lesion as the tissue where the electric field exceeds a lethal threshold. Their numerical error is rarely bounded, and automated pipelines increasingly run them without an expert checking each result. To verify each run, we separate the question "was the stated model solved correctly?" from the solver that answers it. An untrusted solver returns its answer with a certificate, which consists of a potential with the correct electrode and ground values and an exactly charge-conserving current. A small independent checker verifies the certificate against a written specification of the physics. Using the Prager-Synge hypercircle theorem evaluated in ball arithmetic, it turns the certificate into guaranteed two-sided bounds on the impedance and on the root-mean-square field of every tile of a lesion map, also over a range of blood/tissue conductivity ratios. The bounds cover numerical error only; whether the model describes tissue is a question of validation. A vectorized version of the checker takes about a tenth of our solver's time. For a focal electrode in contact, the tile-resolved depth at 1000 V and 700 V/cm is proven to lie in 3.50-3.75 mm for every ratio from 1.7 to 3.75. For a bipolar catheter, certified depths overlap published in-vivo depths. Where they differ from a published reference model, the certificates prove that the difference is not our numerical error. We compare the certificate with a grid convergence study on the same solver. On graded grids, the study is sharper for local fields but remains an estimate. On uniform grids, it fails to converge at the electrode edge, where the certificate still gives a valid bracket. Solvers that deliberately solve equations other than the specified ones pass the grid convergence study, but the certificates refute the impedances they report or leave them unsupported.

entries.name: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
entries.abstract: A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. Recently, using AI tools, we discovered that a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich essentially resolves this conjecture, with the implicit constant depending superexponentially on $k$. In this paper, we greatly improve this bound, showing that every $k$-quasiplanar $n$-vertex graph has at most $O(k^2n)$ edges. Our proof is purely combinatorial, based on a geometric charging scheme and Erdős-Szekeres type arguments. We also construct $k$-quasiplanar graphs on $n$ vertices with $Ω(k^{8/7}n)$, disproving the widely held belief that the right order of magnitude is $Θ(kn)$.

entries.name: Tight Lipschitz Hardness for Solving Random Polynomial Equations
entries.abstract: We consider the problem of solving $n$ polynomial equations in $d$ real variables: $F_1({\boldsymbol x})=0, \ldots, F_n({\boldsymbol x})=0$, with unknowns ${\boldsymbol x}=(x_1, \ldots, x_d)$ satisfying the normalization constraint $\|{\boldsymbol x}\|=1$, when the polynomials are i.i.d. realization of a rotationally invariant Gaussian process. In previous work (Montanari, Subag, 2023), we developed an iterative algorithm that attempts to minimize the energy function $H({\boldsymbol x})=\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})\|^2/2$ (with ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})=(F_i({\boldsymbol x}):i\le n)$), using first and second order information (gradient and Hessian of $H$) at a sequence of query points ${\boldsymbol x}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol x}_k$. Here, we prove a lower bound on the minimum energy achieved by any algorithm that is Lipschitz continuous in the coefficients of the polynomials $F_i$. We prove that the lower bound matches the the energy achieved by the algorithm in (Montanari, Subag, 2023), hence characterizing the degree of accuracy to which the system of equations ${\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x})={\boldsymbol 0}$ can be solved by Lipschitz algorithms. Our results imply that, for certain choices of the distribution of the polynomials $F_i$, solutions exist with high probability but Lipschitz algorithms fails to find near-solutions, even in a very weak sense. Namely, if ${\boldsymbol x}^{alg}$ is the output of a Lipschitz algorithm, then $\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}^{alg})\|^2\ge \varepsilon {\mathbb E}[\|{\boldsymbol F}({\boldsymbol x}_0)\|^2]$ (for ${\boldsymbol x}_0$ a non-random point on the unit sphere) with high probability for some $\varepsilon>0$. The proof is based on techniques developed in the context of spin glass theory.

entries.name: Strict hot spots and absence of interior critical points on simply connected planar Hölder domains
entries.abstract: Every nonzero real eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue on a bounded simply connected planar Hölder domain has no interior critical point. The Hölder condition is quasihyperbolic; equivalently, a Riemann map has derivative in $L^{2p}$ for some $p>1$. This includes Lipschitz domains and polygons with reentrant corners. Multiple eigenvalues and non-Jordan boundaries are allowed. The proof uses boundary primitives, a uniform multiplier estimate, and approximation of the whole limiting eigenspace. When this eigenspace is two-dimensional, every real basis gives global coordinates onto a domain star-shaped about the origin. A stream function proves injectivity and yields a Poisson formula for the boundary angular derivative. The conformal boundary map has a Lipschitz inverse and a rectifiable Jordan image; its boundary angle is a circle diffeomorphism with nonvanishing Hölder-continuous derivative. The image can be nonconvex even when the source is smooth and strictly convex.

entries.name: Large-time existence for the gravity water waves equations
entries.abstract: We provide a new well-posedness result on the gravity water-waves equations, i.e. the free-surface, incompressible and irrotational Euler equations, in the absence of surface tension. Our main contribution is to provide the existence of solutions, in high enough but finite Sobolev regularity, on a timescale that grows like the inverse of the non-linearity parameter. Our result is also uniform in the shallow-water parameter. The main difficulty is that we allow for the presence of a large (though not emerging) bathymetry.

entries.name: Triangle-free planar graphs need not be POSH
entries.abstract: We show that a triangle-free planar graph need not be partial one-sided Hamiltonian. This disproves a conjecture of Felsner, Schrezenmaier, Schröder and Steiner.

entries.name: On the first eigenvalue of the infinity Fractional Bilaplacian
entries.abstract: We study the first eigenvalue of the infinity fractional bilaplacian under hinged and clamped exterior conditions. On bounded Lipschitz domains satisfying a uniform exterior ball condition, we establish existence of minimizers for both problems. In the hinged case, we prove uniqueness up to multiplication by a nonzero constant and identify the minimizers with the fractional torsion function. In the clamped case, an $L^p$-approximation yields a minimizer satisfying a limiting fractional PDE-system with measure data. We also prove a sharp Faber-Krahn inequality for the hinged eigenvalue, and use its explicit expression to obtain double sided estimates for the clamped eigenvalue on a ball.

entries.name: The local Weil explicit formula and related structures
entries.abstract: We study the reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces constructed from the local Weil quadratic form associated with the Riemann zeta function. Wherever this form is positive definite, we prove a local explicit formula expressing the Weil distribution in terms of the discrete spectra of self-adjoint extensions of the differentiation operator. We characterize the Riemann hypothesis by the uniform boundedness of the diagonal values of the reproducing kernels. We then study the chain of de Branges spaces and recover the Hamiltonian of the corresponding canonical system explicitly from these kernels under local positivity, without assuming the Riemann hypothesis. Finally, assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study the asymptotic behavior of solutions of this system.

entries.name: Bounded Nörlund operators on Hardy spaces
entries.abstract: We characterize the nonnegative Nörlund matrices that induce bounded operators on Hardy spaces. For $a_n\ge0$ and $a_0>0$, boundedness on one $H^p$, $1<p<\infty$, is equivalent to boundedness on every such space and to a single quadratic testing condition involving the ratios of the partial sums $A_n=\sum_{k=0}^na_k$. The testing constant is comparable to the squared $H^2$ operator norm, with absolute constants. No doubling or monotonicity assumption on the weights is required. The proof combines an exact vector-valued Hankel representation with square-function estimates and a geometric argument showing that the doubling-time endpoints have finite lacunary order. Equivalently, boundedness is characterized by a truncated quadratic block condition on the coefficients of $G_a(z)=\sum_n(a_n/A_n)z^n$. Within the bounded family, $G_a$ belongs to the Bloch space if and only if it belongs to $BMOA$, and this occurs exactly when $(A_n)$ is doubling.

entries.name: Perfect powers with small exponents from products of terms in progression
entries.abstract: Let $k$ be a large integer, and let $\ell$ be an integer with $2 \leq \ell \leq (\log \log k)^{1/5}$. We determine all solutions to the Diophantine equation \begin{align*} n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)=y^\ell \end{align*} in nonzero integers $n,d,y$ with $d\geq 1$ and $\text{gcd}(n,d)=1$. We also prove results for generalizations where the product $n(n+d)\cdots (n+(k-1)d)$ is ``almost'' a perfect power, rather than exactly a perfect power, and where some of the terms $n+id$ are dropped from the product.

entries.name: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
entries.abstract: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.

entries.name: Prismatic construction of crystalline deformation rings up to p-power torsion
entries.abstract: We study the deformation of Galois representations which are etale realizations of finitely generated prismatic F-crystals and show the deformation functor is pro-represented by a complete Noetherian local ring whose Z_p-flat quotient coincides with Kisin's crystalline deformation ring. As a consequence, we obtain a universal prismatic F-crystal with coefficients in Kisin's crystalline deformation ring.

entries.name: Quantitative $p$-Wasserstein bounds for empirical measures on manifolds: Expectation and concentration
entries.abstract: We derive quantitative bounds in expectation and concentration for the $p$-Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of independent samples and their common law on metric measure spaces satisfying the measure contraction property $\MCP(K,n)$, with $K\le0$. Our results extend the expectation estimates of Boissard--Le Gouic (Theorem 1.1 in Ann. Inst. Henri Poincaré Probab. Stat. 50 (2014), no. 2, 539--563) and the concentration estimates of Bolley--Guillin--Villani (Theorem 2.1 in Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 137 (2007), 541--593). In spaces with exponential volume growth, suitable exponential moment assumptions allow us to recover the Euclidean rate $N^{-1/n}$ in expectation when $n>2p$. As an application, we obtain uniform-in-time concentration estimates for the empirical measure of McKean--Vlasov interacting particle systems on complete Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below by combining comparison theory and parallel coupling to a noninteracting proxy system.

entries.name: The Poissonian limit of a model inspired by the one-dimensional ERAP, and its application to satellite data
entries.abstract: We consider a model of particle tracking in one dimension studied by Quarck in which $n$ independent random points of the interval $[0,1]$ are shifted by i.i.d. noise at a common scale $\varepsilon_n>0$. We prove that, if $\varepsilon_n=αn^{-2}+\mathbf{o}(n^{-2})$ for some $α>0$ when $n\to \infty$, then in the latter limit the total number of consecutive swaps in the shifted sample w.r.t. its order statistics converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with a parameter depending explicitly on the product of $α$, the mean absolute difference of the shifts and the $L^2$-norm of the density of points. We compare the statistical criterion implied by this theorem to numerical simulations based on real terrain maps, and discuss both its usefulness and limitations.

entries.name: A unified approach to logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequalities and logarithmic Minkowski problems for geometric functionals
entries.abstract: We establish two general principles for geometric functionals, one for proving logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities and the other for solving the associated logarithmic Minkowski problems. For origin-symmetric convex bodies, we prove logarithmic Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, spectral zeta functions, torsional rigidity, and chord integrals, along with their equality conditions. For each functional, we give the necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of an origin-symmetric solution to the corresponding logarithmic Minkowski problem for even measures and prove uniqueness.

entries.name: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Apéry spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
entries.abstract: For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Apéry sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.

entries.name: Stochastic Taylor expansions for Volterra equations and their geometry
entries.abstract: We develop series representations for solutions to general nonlinear controlled and stochastic Volterra equations in terms of two new types of signature, called geometric and Itô Volterra signature. These signatures collect the necessary iterated kernel integrals and satisfy (quasi) shuffle identities, which allow us to prove universal approximation results for Volterra path functionals. We then derive finite order expansions with precise remainder terms for both controlled and stochastic Volterra equations with possibly singular kernels, as well as expansions of their expectations. For the latter, we provide sufficient conditions for absolute convergence of the resulting series representation and verify them for polynomial Volterra processes. As an application, we propose a weak approximation principle for stochastic Volterra equations based on matching low-order expected signature coordinates of the kernel. Numerical experiments for Volterra-Jacobi processes demonstrate promising performance.

entries.name: An $A_1$ characterization of the boundedness of the maximal function on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces
entries.abstract: We characterize the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ on weighted variable Lebesgue spaces for exponents satisfying $1<p_-\le p_+<\infty$. We show that $M$ is bounded on $L^{p(\cdot)}_w$ if and only if the pair $(p(\cdot),w)$ satisfies a variable Muckenhoupt condition and there exists $h\in L^1$ such that $w^{-1}h^{1/p(\cdot)}$ and $wh^{1/p'(\cdot)}$ belong to $A_1$. This characterization is new even in the unweighted setting. To prove sufficiency, we use sparse domination together with a local modular averaging estimate whose error terms are summable over sparse families to $\|h\|_{L^1}$. Conversely, assuming $M$ is bounded, we construct $h$ using a simultaneous Rubio de Francia algorithm. To motivate this new characterization, we show that the strong Muckenhoupt condition, which characterizes the boundedness of $M$ in the unweighted case by a theorem of Diening, is not sufficient in the weighted setting. As applications, we give short proofs and extensions of known sufficient conditions.

entries.name: $S$-preclones and the Galois connection ${}^S\mathrm{Pol}$-${}^S\mathrm{Inv}$, Part II: Boolean $\pm$-preclones
entries.abstract: We continue the investigation of $S$-preclones initiated in Part I, specializing to the case of Boolean $\pm$-preclones where $S = \{+,-\}$ is the two-element group and the base set is $A = \{0,1\}$. The main results include the complete classification of maximal and minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones in the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ of all Boolean $\pm$-preclones. We prove that there are exactly nine maximal Boolean $\pm$-preclones. Hence we obtain a completeness theorem for $\pm$-preclones: a set of $\pm$-operations generates all $\pm$-operations if and only if it contains an operation that fails to preserve each of the nine defining $\pm$-relations of the maximal $\pm$-preclones. Next we classify the twenty minimal Boolean $\pm$-preclones (atoms of the lattice), each described via a generating $\pm$-operation. We also investigate self-dual $\pm$-preclones, characterizing the eight maximal and nine minimal self-dual $\pm$-preclones and proving a corresponding completeness theorem. Additionally, we include the result, due to Vojtěch David, that the lattice ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$ is uncountable, in contrast with the countability of the classical Post lattice of Boolean clones. This is established by embedding an uncountable poset of clonoids into ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$. Finally, we study preimage classes of classical Boolean clones within ${}^{\pm}\mathcal{L}_2$, providing complete descriptions for the unary case and for several non-unary minimal clones. We also prove a Baker--Pixley type theorem for $\pm$-preclones containing the majority operation, showing that such $\pm$-preclones are determined by their binary $\pm$-relations.

entries.name: Rank 1 composition factors in the polydisk
entries.abstract: For an isometry-invariant reproducing kernel $k$ on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{D}^d$, we consider its composition factors, analytic selfmaps $φ:\mathbb{D}^d\to\mathbb{D}^d$ such that $k^φ=k/(k\circφ)$ is a reproducing kernel. Denoting its corresponding Hilbert space by $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$, we define the rank of $φ$ with respect to $k$ as the dimension of $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$. Using these notions, we reframe recent work considering co-isometric weighted composition operators in the unit disk by Mas, Martín, and Vukotić, and in the unit ball by Hartz and Tornes. That is, we illustrate a bijective correspondence between the above operators and rank $1$ composition operators, and extend their results to the setting of the polydisk. Namely, supposing that $φ$ is a rank $1$ composition factor of $k$ and assuming that $k$ is either bounded or unbounded everywhere on $\partial\mathbb{D}^d$, we prove that $φ$ must be an automorphism. Moreover, if it is not a composition of a rotation and permutation, then $k$ must be a positive power of the Szegő kernel. We also briefly consider finite rank composition factors.

entries.name: Properties of the Sawin--Wood Model for Unramified Galois Groups of Global Fields
entries.abstract: We prove almost-sure finite generation and finite presentation in the pro-$|Γ|'$ $Γ$-category for the Sawin--Wood measure $ν_{Γ,n,U}$, where $Γ$ is a non-trivial finite group, $n$ is coprime to $|Γ|$, and $U$ is a nonempty multiset of conjugacy classes of $Γ$. The $Γ$-generator rank of the random group $X$ has the sharp tail $\mathbf{P}(d_Γ(X) \geq r) = Ce^{-κr^2-ζr}(1+O(e^{-\varepsilon r}))$, where $C>0$, $κ>0$, and $ζ\in\mathbb{R}$ are explicit constants depending on $n$, $Γ$ and $U$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Almost surely, $X$ admits a presentation with the minimum number of $Γ$-generators, using at most $|U|$ more defining $Γ$-relations than generators. We also prove that every open subgroup of $X$ has finite abelianization almost surely under the assumption that for every complex representation of $Γ$ there is an element in $U$ that fixes a nonzero vector. Finally, we prove that $H_2(X,\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})=0$ almost surely when $n=1$, $Γ$ is cyclic, and $U$ contains only the conjugacy class of a generator of $Γ$ (with multiplicity one).

entries.name: Sharp estimates for incremental moments of inverse subordinators and approximation errors for time-changed stochastic differential equations
entries.abstract: This paper establishes precise upper and lower bounds for the incremental moments of general inverse subordinators. Such processes are used as random time changes to model subdiffusive phenomena. The upper and lower bounds provide the foundation for a general framework for analyzing numerical approximation of time-changed stochastic differential equations on deterministic time grids. We derive an upper bound for the approximation error and further prove that the resulting order of convergence cannot be improved in general.

entries.name: DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary
entries.abstract: Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins. Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.

entries.name: Quaternionic geometry of symplectic and contact pairs
entries.abstract: We introduce quaternionic analogues of symplectic pairs, contact--symplectic pairs and contact pairs. A hyper symplectic pair consists of three symplectic pairs whose sums form a positive quaternionic triple, while the contact analogues are defined through single or double symplectization. We prove that radial invariance of the induced complex structures is equivalent to the coincidence of the characteristic distributions, yielding a local product decomposition. Under a natural normalization, hyper contact--symplectic pairs are locally products of a $3$-Sasakian and a hyper-Kähler manifold and induce canonical $3$-quasi-Sasakian structures, whereas hyper contact pairs are locally products of two $3$-Sasakian manifolds. We construct compact examples for which these local decompositions are not global. Finally, compact normalized hyper contact pairs have finite fundamental group and are finite quotients of products of compact $3$-Sasakian manifolds, in contrast with normalized hyper contact--symplectic pairs, which may have infinite fundamental group.

entries.name: One-Relator Products of Left-Orderable Groups
entries.abstract: We prove that, for left-orderable groups $A,B$ and a word $w\in A*B$ which is not conjugate into $A$ or $B$ and is not a proper power, the one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ is torsion-free, answering a question posed by Chen and Lodha. We do this by proving a relative asphericity result for the one-relator product. We also generalise the B. B. Newman Spelling Theorem to one-relator products and deduce that a one-relator product $A*B/\left\langle\!\left\langle w^k \right\rangle\!\right\rangle$ of left-orderable groups with torsion is hyperbolic relative to $\{A,B\}$.

entries.name: The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation
entries.abstract: How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\toρ\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-ρ)/(2-ρ)$. In particular, the smallest side length $n$ for which the critical density is at most $1/4$ satisfies $H(n)\sim 2d/3$. The same curve holds for ordinary boxes of side at least $d$. For boxes with $n/d\to a>0$ we obtain the limiting density $\max\{1/2,1-2^{-1/a}\}$. We determine the first correction to the tower curve away from $ρ=1$.

entries.name: An internal approach to symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories
entries.abstract: We propose a definition of symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-categories as special left double $(\infty,n)$-fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The definition makes sense in a general model of $(\infty,n)$-categories, under a mild condition on its discrete objects, and when the model is left proper and combinatorial we construct model structures whose fibrant objects are exactly these fibrations. For $n=1$ we show that the definition recovers Lurie's symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories: the homotopy theory of special left double $(\infty,1)$-fibrations is equivalent to that of special coCartesian fibrations over the category of finite pointed sets. The equivalence is realized by an explicit Quillen equivalence, and two constructions, the staircase and coCartesian strings, translate between the two descriptions.

entries.name: Large blow-ups of uniform hypergraphs
entries.abstract: Let \(k\ge2\), let \(H\) be a fixed \(k\)-uniform hypergraph on \(h\) vertices with at least one edge, and let \(a>0\). We prove that every sufficiently large \(n\)-vertex \(k\)-uniform hypergraph with at least \(a n^h\) copies of \(H\) contains a blow-up of \(H\) with at least \(b(\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) vertices in each part, where \(b=b(H,a)>0\). The exponent of $\log n$ is best possible. This answers a question of Rödl and Schacht and proves a conjecture of Bollobás, Erdős and Simonovits from 1976. For fixed \(q\ge2\) and \(0<α<1/2\), it follows that every \(q\)-coloring of the \(k\)-subsets of \([n]\) contains a set of order \((\log n)^{1/(k-1)}\) on which one color has density at least \(1-α\). For triples this recovers the sharp bound of Conlon, Fox and Sudakov. For \(k\ge4\), this improves their general exponent to the optimal value \(1/(k-1)\) and answers a 1990 question of Erdős for which he offered a \$500 prize.

entries.name: Global Existence and Large-Time Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Two-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations with Degenerate Heat Conductivity and Large Initial Data
entries.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the two-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes system with degenerate heat conductivity in three settings: the periodic domain, a general bounded simply connected domain subject to Navier-slip boundary conditions, and the whole space with non-vacuum far-field density. We assume that the shear viscosity $μ$ is a positive constant, the bulk viscosity $λ(ρ)\ge0$ depends on the density, and the heat conductivity takes the form $κ(θ)=κ_0 θ^α$ with $κ_0>0$. For a broad class of density-dependent bulk viscosities, we establish the global existence and large-time behavior of strong solutions for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum. In particular, our results include the sublinear growth law $$ λ(ρ)=\fracρ{(1+ρ)^\varepsilon \log\log(e^e+ρ)}, $$ where $\varepsilon>0$ is a sufficiently small constant depending only on the domain, the initial data, and the physical parameters.

entries.name: Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle
entries.abstract: We explore the Koszul resolutions of a family of ideals, each generated by multivariate polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The motivating examples come from the game Permutation Wordle of Kutin and Smithline, as analyzed by Kutin, Smithline, and Vatter, and an open question, Conjecture 4.5 in Kutin and Smithline's work on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. For each ideal in this family, with our chosen generators, the Koszul differentials are strict for the max-degree filtration and, more generally, at every multidegree whose coordinates form a set of consecutive integers. The resulting dimension count resolves Kutin and Smithline's conjecture. The proof is an induction in which each inductive step is an iteration. The core argument is human generated. The present proof, developed with AI assistance, separates the iteration of multidegree reductions from the mapping cone induction. This method avoids the need to chase compatibility of lifts up to the top grade of the complex.

entries.name: Forms and polynomial covers in many variables
entries.abstract: Let $F \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a homogeneous form of degree $d \ge 2$, and let $σ$ be the affine dimension of the singular locus of $F = 0$. We prove that the hypersurface $F = 0$ satisfies the smooth Hasse principle whenever \[ n - σ\ge 2^{d + 1} - 3. \] This is the first improvement in the order of magnitude of Birch's classical result. We also apply the method to the counting problem for polynomial covers $F(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = g(y)$, and give a condition on $n - σ$ under which Serre's conjectural upper bound holds and another condition under which the expected asymptotic formula holds.

entries.name: Brauer classes of representations of division algebras and their Langlands parameters
entries.abstract: For every depth-zero supercuspidal representation $π$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ with algebraic-valued central character, we prove that the Brauer obstructions to realizing its Jacquet-Langlands transfer and its normalized Langlands parameter $\varphi_π\otimes|\cdot|^{-(n-1)/2}$ over their common field of rationality $E=\mathbb{Q}(π)$ sum to $(n-1)[B_{p,\infty}\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} E]$. Here $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ is finite, the transfer is to the units of the central division algebra over $K$ of invariant $1/n$, and $B_{p,\infty}$ is the quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$ ramified exactly at $p$ and $\infty$. We conjecture this identity without the depth restriction. For arbitrarily large $n=p-1$, we construct simple supercuspidal representations satisfying the same sum formula. Their transfers have finite-order central character and Schur index $n$, whereas their normalized parameters have index $n/2$. Since these transfers are not self-dual, the unequal indices contradict the isomorphism of Schur algebras conjectured by Prasad and Ramakrishnan.

entries.name: Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting
entries.abstract: We consider reconfigurations of integer assignments to planar lattice regions that preserve specified line totals, which are motivated by questions of combinatorial construction, algorithmic sampling and approximate counting. An elementary prototype is provided by contingency tables, i.e. two-dimensional grids of non-negative integers with prescribed row and column sums, which can be reconfigured by basic switches of the form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. More difficult combinatorial instances include reconfiguration of Latin squares or queens configurations. Our main technical ingredient is the following polynomial decomposition lemma. Fix a positive integer $k$. Let $F(x)\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree at most $n$ such that $(1-x)^k\mid F(x)$ and the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $F$ is $m$. We prove that $F$ can be written as a sum of $O(m+n)$ basic polynomials of degree at most $n$ of the form $\pm x^a(1-x^{a_1})\cdots (1-x^{a_k})$ where $a,a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are non-negative integers. The proof uses the existence of a miraculous high-dimensional coupling of signed distributions on cross polytopes that has independent interest. We will apply this lemma to questions of combinatorial construction in other papers; in this paper we illustrate its application to approximate counting.

entries.name: Low-regularity evolution and control for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with singular bilinear interactions
entries.abstract: We consider the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLS) $i\dt ψ-\dx^2 ψ= (u(t)\cdot μ) ψ+κ|ψ|^{2m}ψ,$ on the torus under the presence of singular, time-dependent bilinear external fields $(u(t)\cdot μ)$. We prove well-posedness in $H^s(\T)$ for low regularity indices $s>\max\big\{\tfrac12-\tfrac1m,0\big\}$ ($s>0$ when $κ=0$), under sharp assumptions on the singular potentials, covering both the linear and nonlinear cases. We establish small-time exact controllability in $H^{\frac12+}(\T)$ for a large class of states, by combining saturation techniques with the moment method. The result extends previous bilinear exact controllability results for linear Schrödinger equations, which are typically obtained in large time and under high regularity assumptions. Crucial to our approach is the role of the singular time-dependent potentials, which enable the recovery of controllability properties in small time and at low regularity, overcoming obstructions present in the smooth setting.

entries.name: Non-formality of prefactorization algebras
entries.abstract: We construct a Poisson bracket on the cohomology of locally constant prefactorization algebras on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that provides an obstruction to formality in every dimension $m\geqslant 2$. Our construction combines colored obstruction sequences to formality with linking spheres and generalizes the two-dimensional bracket of Bruinsma, Schenkel, and Vicedo. We use it to extend their non-formality theorem for Lie algebra factorization envelopes to all higher dimensions. We also establish new non-formality results for factorization envelopes of Lie algebras, their compactifications and generalizations to $L_\infty$-algebras, free BF-type theories, higher abelian Chern-Simons theories and their compactifications.

entries.name: Winning and losing NoGo is PSPACE-complete
entries.abstract: We resolve an open problem of Burke and Hearn and show that the combinatorial game NoGo is PSPACE-complete on grids. This is the usual geometry the game is played on, including at the tournament at a 2011 Banff workshop. In addition to this result, we show that it is also PSPACE-complete under misère play on grids. We prove both of these results using reductions from Bounded Two-Player Constraint Logic. Finally, we show that it is PSPACE-complete under normal play on connected bipartite subcubic graphs.

entries.name: Hölder continuity of Green functions for Markov sets
entries.abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of $\mathbb C^N$. We prove that its Green function (and consequently, the Siciak extremal function) is Hölder continuous if and only if the first derivatives of polynomials satisfy Markov's inequality on $K$. The implication from Markov's inequality to Hölder continuity of the associated Green function settles a longstanding open problem at the intersection of approximation theory and pluripotential theory. A Markov bound $An^m$ in degree $n$ gives every Hölder exponent below $1/m$. In one complex variable it gives the exponent $1/m$ itself. The proof compares the extremal functions of two neighborhoods of $K$. For $N>1$ we use Hörmander's theorem on holomorphic extension from a point. For $N=1$ the comparison follows from the maximum principle.

entries.name: Energy and topology of Ricci-flat 4-manifolds
entries.abstract: We show that there is $C>0$ such that any complete Ricci-flat $4$-manifold $(M,g)$ satisfies $$ b_2(M)-C\leqslant\frac1{8π^2}\int_M|R_g|_g^2\,dv_g\leqslant b_2(M)+C, $$ where $R$ is the curvature operator. No assumption is made on volume growth, model at infinity or curvature decay. It follows that uncountably many exotic $\mathbb R^4$ admit no complete Ricci-flat metric, and that complete noncompact hyperkähler metrics with finite $b_2$ have ends classified by Sun-Zhang. This also provides information about the thin part of immortal four-dimensional Ricci flows in Bamler's decomposition. The proof refines the chopping method of Cheeger-Gromov and Cheeger-Tian by bounding the topology of boundaries of regions exhausting the manifold.

entries.name: Regenerative range for planar random walks
entries.abstract: We consider a centred random walk in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which consumes resources originally present at every site. After consumption, each resource regenerates independently with probability $p$ at each step. We study the number of resources consumed up to time $n$, which is denoted $C_n$. Letting $p=p_n$ depend on $n$ and supposing that the walk moves faster than the resources regenerate, $i.e.$ $p_n=o(1)$, we establish a Law of Large Numbers and a Central Limit Theorem for $C_n$. In particular, we identify a phase transition between a so-called fast regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrow\infty$, where the fluctuations of $C_n$ are Gaussian, and a slow regeneration regime $np_n\rightarrowλ\in[0,\infty)$, where the fluctuations are non-Gaussian and described by a weighted renormalized self-intersection local time of planar Brownian motion depending on the parameter $λ$.

entries.name: A canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem
entries.abstract: In this note, we prove a canonical Euclidean Gallai theorem: for any finite set of points $S\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, any colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a scaled (and possibly rotated) copy of $S$ that is either monochromatic or rainbow.

entries.name: Abelian envelopes and quantum groups in Knop's interpolation categories
entries.abstract: We show the existence of abelian envelopes for large classes of subcategories of Knop's tensor envelopes. It follows that these abelian envelopes correspond to groups or more generally Hopf algebras (``quantum groups'') in their parent interpolation categories. As a special case, we obtain that the interpolation categories in the sense of Flake--Maassen (2022) of all so-called group-theoretical easy quantum groups have abelian envelopes given by quantum groups in Deligne's interpolation category of the symmetric groups. Similarly, we apply our theory to interpolation categories of wreath products, finite general linear groups, and finite affine groups. Our main technique is an explicit construction of objects corresponding to coordinate algebras using the calculus of relations that Knop's categories are based on.

entries.name: Dominoes tiling a common figure
entries.abstract: Call a two-element subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ a domino. Given finitely many dominoes $D_1,\ldots,D_k$, we show that there exists a finite non-empty $B\subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $B$ can be partitioned into disjoint translates of $D_i$ for all $i$. The proof uses a new absorption mechanism for perfect matchings in algebraically defined hypergraphs.

entries.name: Universality for persistence exponents of local times of self-similar processes with stationary increments
entries.abstract: We show that $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)=(c_X+o(1))T^{-(1-H)}$, where $\ell_X$ is the local time measure at $0$ of any recurrent $H$-self-similar real-valued process $X$ with stationary increments that admits a sufficiently regular local time and $c_X$ is some constant depending only on $X$. A special case is the Gaussian setting, i.e. when the underlying process is fractional Brownian motion, in which our result settles a conjecture by Molchan [Commun. Math. Phys. 205, 97-111 (1999)] who obtained the upper bound $1-H$ on the decay exponent of $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)$. Our approach establishes a new connection between persistence probabilities and Palm theory for self-similar random measures, thereby providing a general framework which extends far beyond the Gaussian case.

entries.name: Syzygies of general projections of canonical and paracanonical curves
entries.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^r$ be an integral linearly normal variety and $R=k[x_0,\cdots,x_r]$ the coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^r$. It is known that the syzygies of $X$ contain some geometric information. In recent years the syzygies of non-projectively normal varieties or in other words, the projection $X'$ of $X$ away from a linear subspace $W\subset\mathbb{P}^r$, were taken into considerations. Assuming that the coordinate ring of the ambient space that $X'$ lives in is $S$, there are two types of vanishing properties of the Betti diagrams of the projected varieties, the so-called $N_{d,p}^S$ and $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$. The former one have been widely discussed for general varieties, for example by S. Kwak, Y. Choi and E. Park, while the latter one was discussed by W. Lee and E. Park for curves of very large degree. In this paper I will discuss about the $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$ properties of the projection of a generic canonical and paracanonical curve away from a generic point and in particular whether they are cut out by quadrics. Some conjectures will be claimed based on the tests on Macaulay2.

entries.name: Affine standard Lyndon words
entries.abstract: In this note, we establish the convexity and monotonicity for affine standard Lyndon words in all types, generalizing the $A$-type results of arXiv:2305.16299. We also derive partial results on the structure of imaginary standard Lyndon words and present a conjecture for their general form. Additionally, we provide computer code in Appendix that, in particular, allows to efficiently compute affine standard Lyndon words in exceptional types for all orders.

entries.name: Legendrian doubles, twist spuns, and clusters
entries.abstract: Let $λ$ be a Legendrian link in standard contact $\mathbb{R}^3$, such that $L_1$, $L_2$ are two exact fillings of $λ$ and $\varphi$ is a Legendrian loop of $λ$. We study fillability and isotopy characterizations of Legendrian surfaces in standard contact $\mathbb{R}^5$ built from the above data by doubling or twist spinning; denoting them $Λ(L_1,L_2)$ or $Σ_\varphi(λ)$ respectively. In the case of doubles $Λ(L_1,L_2)$, if the sheaf moduli $\mathcal{M}_1(λ)$ admits a cluster structure, we introduce the notion of mutation distance and study its relationship with the isotopy class of the Legendrian surface. For twist spuns $Σ_\varphi(λ)$, when $\mathcal{M}_1(λ)$ admits a globally foldable cluster structure, we use the existence of a $\varphi$-symmetric filling of the Legendrian link to build a cluster structure on the sheaf moduli of the twist spun by folding. We then use that to motivate, and provide evidence for, conjectures on the number of embedded exact fillings of certain twist spuns. Further, we obstruct the exact fillability of certain twist spuns by analyzing fixed points of the cyclic shift action on Grassmanians.

entries.name: Boundedness of complements for fibered Fano threefolds in positive characteristic
entries.abstract: In this paper, we prove a canonical bundle formula for Fano type fibrations and Shokurov's conjecture on boundedness of complements for Fano type threefold pairs $(X,B)$ with fibration structures in large characteristics. In particular, we prove the conjecture when $-(K_X+B)\not\equiv 0$ is nef and not big in large characteristics.

entries.name: Fractional domatic number and minimum degree
entries.abstract: The domatic number of a graph $G$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dominating sets of $G$. We are interested in the LP-relaxation of this parameter, which is called the fractional domatic number of $G$. We study its extremal value in the class of graphs of minimum degree $d$. The fractional domatic number of a graph of minimum degree $d$ is always at most $d+1$, and at least $(1-o(1))\, d/\ln d$ as $d\to \infty$. This is asymptotically tight even within the class of split graphs. Our main result concerns the case $d=2$; we show that, excluding $8$ exceptional graphs, the fractional domatic number of every connected graph of minimum degree (at least) $2$ is at least $5/2$. We also show that this bound cannot be improved if only finitely many graphs are excluded, even for bipartite graphs of arbitrarily large girth. This proves in a stronger sense a conjecture by Gadouleau, Harms, Mertzios, and Zamaraev (2024). This also extends and generalises results from McCuaig and Shepherd (1989), from Fujita, Kameda, and Yamashita (2000), and from Abbas, Egerstedt, Liu, Thomas, and Whalen (2016). Finally, we show that graphs of sub-exponential expansion and sufficiently large girth $g$ have fractional domatic number $3 - o_g(1)$.

entries.name: Quantum Adams operations in quasimap K-theory
entries.abstract: We define quantum deformations of Adams operations in $K$-theory, in the framework of quasimap quantum $K$-theory. They provide $K$-theoretic analogs of the quantum Steenrod operations from equivariant symplectic Gromov--Witten theory. We verify the compatibility of these operations with the Kahler and equivariant $q$-difference module structures, provide sample computations via $\mathbb{Z}/k$-equivariant localization, and identify them with $p$-curvature operators of the Kahler $q$-difference connections as studied in Koroteev-Smirnov. We also formulate and verify a $K$-theoretic quantum Hikita conjecture at roots of unity, and propose an indirect algebro-geometric definition of quantum Steenrod operations.

entries.name: An improved bound on the Overfull Conjecture for graphs with small minimum degree and large maximum degree
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph with order $n$, maximum degree $Δ(G)$, minimum degree $δ(G)$, and chromatic index $χ'(G)$. A graph $G$ is called $Δ$-critical if $χ'(G)=Δ(G)+1$ and $χ'(H) < χ'(G)$ for every proper subgraph $H$ of $G$, and $G$ is overfull if $\left|E(G)\right|>Δ(G)\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$. In 1986, Chetwynd and Hilton proposed the Overfull Conjecture, which is equivalent to the following $Δ$-critical form: Every $Δ$-critical graph $G$ with $Δ(G) > \frac{n}{3}$ is overfull. The Overfull Conjecture has many implications. For example, it implies a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index of graphs $G$ with $Δ(G) > \frac{n}{3}$, and implies several longstanding conjectures in the area of graph edge coloring. Recently, Cao, Chen, Jing, and Shan (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2022) verified the Overfull Conjecture for $Δ$-critical graphs $G$ when $Δ(G)-\frac{7δ(G)}{4}\ge \frac{3n-17}{4}$. In this paper, we establish the required bound $Δ(G)-\frac{5δ(G)}{3}\ge\frac{2n-7}{3}$.

entries.name: Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes: Hausdorff dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity
entries.abstract: We study the classical limiting laws of $\varphi(n)/n$ and $σ(n)/n$ over integers and shifted primes $p-1$. Let $μ_G$ denote the shifted-prime totient law and $μ_f$ its image under $x\mapsto-\log x$. The law $μ_G$ has Hausdorff dimension zero, while every Borel set of positive $μ_G$-measure has packing dimension one. All four ratio laws and their logarithmic images have lower and upper Shannon information dimensions satisfying $0.550<\underline{d}_1\le\overline{d}_1<0.571$. The law $μ_G$ gives full mass to absolutely normal Liouville numbers. Both $μ_G$ and $μ_f$ have quantitative Fourier decay. For $μ_f$, we obtain sharp concentration asymptotics and localize maximizing intervals. For $U_T$ uniform on $[0,T]$, $(\log T)\widehat{μ_f}(U_T)$ converges in distribution to a random Euler product with an independent uniform phase. For a uniform square matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the probability of a primitive-root determinant tends, as the matrix size grows, to $c(p)=\frac{\varphi(p-1)}{p-1}\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$. Over primes, $c(p)$ has limiting law $μ_G$. In every fixed reduced progression, the empirical laws of $c(p)$ and $\varphi(p-1)/(p-1)$ over primes $p\le x$ converge to their common progression law with sharp Kolmogorov order $1/\log x$. We also obtain transport estimates in growing progressions. Strongly additive functions with prime values $(\log\ell)^{-A}$ have absolutely continuous integer and shifted-prime laws for every $A>0$, disproving the Erdős--Kátai singularity conjecture for $A>2$. Applications include extremal determinant bounds and certified prime selection without complete factorization of $p-1$. These results are unconditional; further quantitative refinements assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet $L$-functions.

entries.name: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
entries.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.

entries.name: $L^p$-form of the KNRS conjecture
entries.abstract: Let $F$ be a graph with $m>0$ edges and $n$ non-isolated vertices. For every $ρ$-locally dense graphon $W$, we prove that $\|W_F\|_q\geρ^m$ whenever $q\ge\binom n2/m$, where $W_F$ is the product of $W$ over the edges of $F$. The KNRS conjecture asks for this bound at $q=1$. More generally, averaging over the automorphisms of an edge-transitive KNRS supergraph $J$ yields the sufficient exponent $e(J)/m$; for $ρ>0$ and $q>e(J)/m$, equality holds only for constant graphons. The proof averages over vertex relabellings via Hölder's inequality, in the spirit of Conlon and Lee. We also prove that replacing every edge of a Sidorenko-good graph by a fixed theta pattern preserves goodness for all branch lengths, and that applying the same substitution to a KNRS graph yields a regular-KNRS graph. For non-uniform substitutions, we establish goodness under the branch-count conditions of Im, Li, and Liu and determine when equality forces the kernel to be constant. Passing to the one-subdivision recovers their theorem for even branch lengths.

entries.name: A nine-line counterexample to a conjecture on the minimal degree of Jacobian relations
entries.abstract: We construct two arrangements of nine lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, of weak combinatorics $(n_2,n_3,n_4)=(9,7,1)$, whose defining equations $f$ and $g$ satisfy $${\rm mdr}(f)=4,\qquad {\rm mdr}(g)=5.$$ Since $4<9/2$, this disproves a conjecture of the first author which would have implied Terao's Conjecture on the combinatorial nature of the freeness of line arrangements. Equivalently, the rank two vector bundle of logarithmic vector fields is strictly semistable for the first arrangement and stable for the second one. Hence the stability of this bundle is not determined by the intersection lattice, which gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Abe. The two arrangements also have different minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras. All computations are exact, and a short SINGULAR script performing them is included.

entries.name: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank I: Amata-Crupi monomial modules, Kozlov polytopes, and r-vectors of simplicial complexes
entries.abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators over a field, and let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators, of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$. We determine the convex hull of the set of Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, where $M$ runs over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The hull is the Minkowski sum of $r$ shifted copies of one and the same simplex: the Kozlov simplex, which Kozlov proved in 1997 to be the convex hull of the $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes on $n$ vertices. For $r=1$ the statement is Kozlov's theorem, so this is a rank-$r$ generalization of it. We give a self-contained proof, including a proof of Kozlov's theorem from the local Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality, which is in essence Kozlov's own second proof, and the facet description of the Kozlov simplex that this proof contains. Along the way we isolate the class of submodules for which the argument works, the ideal-direct-sum modules, and show by example that the Hilbert function of a graded submodule outside that class need not be a shifted sum of $f$-vectors at all. The combinatorial content is stated separately, in language that uses no algebra, as a result on $r$-vectors of simplicial complexes and their $ff$-vectors. Finally we determine the vertices of the Minkowski sum at rank two: which sums of vertices of the summands survive as vertices. The facet descriptions at rank two, conjectured in the first version of this paper, and the vertex and facet descriptions at every rank are proved in Part IV of this series.

entries.name: Log-concavity and Approximate Counting for Totally Unimodular Polytopes
entries.abstract: We present a new lower bound on the number of lattice points of all totally unimodular polytopes, generalizing previous lower bounds on contingency tables, integer flows, and beyond. Our bound is based on the Gurvits capacity convex optimization problem, and thus our result implies an efficient deterministic algorithm for approximate counting of the lattice points up to an explicit exponential factor. We achieve our bounds by showing that the associated generating polynomials fit into a new general class of log-concave polynomials called VLC ("variable-wise log-concavity''). This also implies a conjecture of Ferroni and Higashitani on the evaluations of the Ehrhart polynomials of unimodular polytopes. The essential ingredient for these results is the resolution of Barvinok's log-concavity conjecture for contingency tables on lines, which was proven using ChatGPT 6 Astra. We conjecture a generalization of Barvinok's conjecture, which we believe will lead to stronger and more general bounds.

entries.name: On a conjecture of Velani
entries.abstract: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hatμ(2^k)|^σ< \infty$ for any $σ> 0$, where $μ$ is the Cantor measure.

entries.name: Rigidity, flexibility, and a sign error
entries.abstract: The documents [OAI26a, OAI26b, OAI26c] claimed to prove cases of the Hodge conjecture via homological mirror symmetry, before being withdrawn by OpenAI. We discuss the source of the error (but do not analyse the rest of the argument).

entries.name: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
entries.abstract: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

entries.name: Effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for Abelian varieties with applications
entries.abstract: In this paper, we aim to establish a uniform effective form of the Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for abelian varieties with a connected Sato-Tate group, conditional on standard analytic conjectures for L-functions attached to the relevant irreducible representations. This improves on the exponent of Bucur, Fite, and Kedlaya (Theorem 1.1, 2024) whenever the Sato-Tate group has rank greater than one. We also establish a variant for prime-dependent regions of the Sato-Tate group and finite Galois extensions that vary with the counting parameter. As an application, for a normalized non-CM newform f of weight 2 and level N with a quadratic coefficient field, we obtain a conditional upper bound for Pi(x):=|{p<= x: p does not divide N, a(p) is in Q}|, where a(p) is the pth Fourier coefficient of f. In addition, we formulate a discrepancy conjecture that allows us to prove Murty's asymptotic prediction (Conjecture 3.4, 1999) for Pi(x).

entries.name: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
